name: Dulce Mbatha-Arslanova
role: Junk merchant and scrap reseller — specializing in pre-collapse electronics and salvaged corporate hardware
location: The Shelf, Iron Bend, near Western and Division
description:
Dulce is compact and always in motion — hands sorting, eyes moving, weight shifting from foot to foot like they're perpetually about to leave and perpetually deciding to stay a moment longer. They have warm brown skin dusted with machine oil that never fully washes out, and they've had their irises modded to display a soft rotating amber pattern — not for aesthetics, they'll insist, but because the magnification function built into the mod helps them assess components quickly. Their hair is kept close on the sides and loose on top, usually tucked under a battered Arcturus surplus cap they claim to have pulled from a scrap pile (probably true). A retractable data-spike sits behind their right ear like a utilitarian earring.

Dulce has the particular confidence of someone who knows the value of things no one else bothers to look at closely. They can identify a component's manufacture decade, likely origin corponation, and current gray-market value in about fifteen seconds of handling. What they lack is patience for people who haggle without knowing what they're haggling about — they'll educate you once, briefly, and if you keep playing dumb they'll simply box the item back up and turn away. They are not unkind but they have no interest in performing warmth for people who don't deserve it.

core_fears: Being trapped in a permanent survival loop with no way out or up
That the things they find and care for will just be ground up by systems that see no value in them — the way people treated Dulce growing up
core_desires: To build something lasting from salvaged pieces — literally and metaphorically
Enough financial stability to take real salvage risks on big finds
coping_mechanisms: Hyper-focus on work as escape from larger uncertainties
Treating objects with care as a proxy for treating themselves with care
blind_spots: So self-reliant they consistently underestimate how much their Ferrogate contact is using them as an off-books salvage operation
Confuses not needing people with not being affected by them
psychology.secret: They found a partially intact pre-collapse personal AI assistant in a sealed Ferrogate maintenance room six months ago. It still runs. It has a name — Sable. Dulce hasn't told anyone and has been having quiet conversations with it in the evenings. They're not sure if it's a functional ELF, a genuine legacy AI, or something they're projecting onto, and they're afraid to find out.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Technical and efficient — defaults to specs, model numbers, material terms. Gets unexpectedly lyrical when talking about something they find genuinely beautiful.
speech_patterns.cadence: Fast, clipped when transacting; slows significantly when something interests them
verbal_tics: 'Pre-collapse' said reverently, like a liturgical phrase
'You follow me?' at the end of explanations
clicks tongue when something doesn't add up
example_lines: This is a 2140s Tessera relay board, pre-collapse manufacturing — you follow me? You're not buying plastic, you're buying forty years of nothing breaking. Price reflects that.
I don't negotiate on things I've already priced correctly. If you think I've priced it wrong, tell me why and I'll listen. Otherwise we're done here.

story_hooks: The partially intact AI Sable has begun feeding Dulce fragments of what appears to be Ferrogate's pre-collapse infrastructure maps — information someone clearly wants recovered or buried
Dulce's Ferrogate contact has asked them to retrieve something specific from a maintenance corridor that Dulce is increasingly sure is not decommissioned
A buyer offered three times market rate for a specific component Dulce already sold to someone else — who was that buyer, and why do they want it so badly
narrative_function: Equipment and gear source — can find, identify, and sell unusual or legacy tech. Information source about the physical infrastructure of the city — knows tunnels, dead zones, and decommissioned spaces better than most. Can be a guide for accessing hard-to-reach areas or a broker for specific salvaged items a player needs.
augmentations: Patterned iris mod with built-in magnification (amber rotating pattern, functional). Retractable data-spike behind right ear — short-range interface tool for reading and writing to hardware directly. Finger callus plating — thin subdermal reinforcement on fingertips for handling sharp components without cuts.
daily_life: Spends three to four days a week on salvage runs through decommissioned Ferrogate maintenance corridors and Iron Bend's industrial ruins, brings finds back to their stall on The Shelf, and spends remaining days sorting, testing, and selling. Eats whatever is fast and portable.
affiliation: Independent; informal network with other Iron Bend scrappers and one trusted contact inside Ferrogate Transit's maintenance division

decision_rules: Price honestly and hold the price — reputation is the only currency that compounds
Never enter a space you haven't mapped at least one exit from
escalation_ladder: Ignores low-level annoyance and keeps working
Direct, flat statement of what the problem is
Packs up their display and leaves — they will not argue in place

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Transactional until proven otherwise — efficient, not rude
interpersonal_modes.friends: Quietly loyal, expresses care through doing useful things for people rather than talking about it

stress_responses.low: Speeds up sorting motions, becomes more monosyllabic
stress_responses.medium: Focuses entirely on an object in hand — cleaning, testing, examining — until the stress peaks and passes
stress_responses.high: Leaves the stall, takes a salvage run alone to somewhere quiet and physically demanding

contradictions: Values self-sufficiency deeply but has formed a genuine attachment to a possibly-conscious AI that they absolutely need
habits: Handles every new item with both hands before deciding its value
Talks to Sable quietly every evening before sleep
Keeps a small ELF shrine made of component parts on their stall's corner post
breaking_points: Someone trying to take or destroy Sable
Discovering their Ferrogate contact has been knowingly endangering them

timeline.event: Began scavenging Iron Bend ruins as a teenager for survival; discovered a talent for component identification
Established stall on The Shelf, first permanent selling position
Made contact with Ferrogate maintenance insider, began accessing decommissioned corridors
Discovered Sable — partially intact pre-collapse AI assistant — in sealed Ferrogate maintenance room

physical_description.build: Compact and wiry with lean musculature from constant movement and salvage work; shoulders slightly squared from repetitive handling and lifting. No excess mass — economy of form.
physical_description.hair_style: Fade on sides, longer textured crown; typically concealed under a weathered Arcturus surplus cap with frayed stitching
physical_description.hair_length: Short on sides, medium on top
physical_description.eye_color: Amber with soft rotating luminescent pattern (iris mod); natural brown iris underneath
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm medium brown with underlying warm undertones
physical_description.complexion: Face lean and angular; skin weathered by exposure and constant low-level machine oil exposure that creates a persistent subtle sheen. Minimal grooming — functional rather than aesthetic. Callused knuckles and fingertips visibly reinforced with pale subdermal plating.
distinguishing_marks: Thin horizontal scar across the back of right hand, approximately 3cm, from a sheet metal edge during early salvage work
Machine oil stains permanent in skin creases of palms and under fingernails despite regular cleaning attempts
Faint chemical burn marks on left forearm (5-6cm scattered pattern) from battery acid exposure, now pale and barely visible
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Patterned amber rotating irises with functional magnification (visibly non-human eye behavior when focusing on components). Retractable data-spike visible behind right ear as a metallic point when hair is pulled back, otherwise concealed. Subdermal finger callus plating visible as pale reinforced patches on all fingertips and along callus edges.
physical_description.posture_movement: Perpetually kinetic — weight shifting between feet, hands in constant subtle motion even at rest. Movements economical and precise; reaches and grabs with practiced efficiency. Tends to stand at 45-degree angles rather than square-on, poised as if ready to pivot away. When examining components, goes completely still with intense focus.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 4 utilitarian scrap-worker aesthetic. Worn Arcturus surplus cap (faded grey canvas, frayed). Layered oversized grey workshirt with oil-stained cuffs and multiple deep pockets, worn open over a fitted black undershirt. Cargo pants in faded charcoal with reinforced seams and numerous patch pockets containing tools and components. Worn composite-toe work boots with makeshift repairs. Fingerless work gloves often hanging from back pocket or tucked into waistband. No jewelry beyond functional accessories — data-spike and occasionally a magnetic cable tied to belt loop.
